newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allied bomb defused near German president's office.
newsitem.headline: Allied bomb defused near German president's office.

text.p: Explosives experts on Thursday defused a World War Two-era bomb near German President Roman Herzog's office after police evacuated about 40 members of his staff, a police spokesman said.

The spokesman said a 300 metre (yard) radius around the site of the bomb, including the Tiergarten park and several major avenues, had to be blocked off for about an hour until technicians could defuse the 500 kg (1,100 lb) device.
"About two hours after the bomb was discovered, it was successfully defused on site," the spokesman said, adding that construction workers had uncovered the bomb while digging at a building site.

Herzog had intended to leave his office anyway around the time of the evacuation to meet with visiting Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and was not in any danger, a spokeswoman from his office said.
The spokeswoman said that this was the second time in a week and a half that a bomb from World War Two had been found near the president's office.
Berlin officials say such evacuations are a relatively common occurrence. They discover about 25 unexploded bombs and up to 6,000 live grenades left by the Allies every year.
